    14	This file constructs the relative relation tower generated by the multiplier window.

    17	index one.  Every later successor is the range of the analogous finite basis-indexed

   172	/-- The recursive high-window relation modules.

   174	Stage zero is the universal first window.  Stage one is the already-landed universal

    10	/-!
    11	# Persistence at every high divisor-scheme window
    12	
    13	The two Grassmannian windows recover an effective degree-`g` divisor `D` on every
    14	field fibre.  The same multiplication argument is not confined to those first two
    15	windows: after replacing `N` by `N + n * S`, the degree budgets only improve.  Thus
    16	the full `S`-window carries `H^0(O(N + n*S - D))` onto the next stage for every `n`.
    17	
    18	This is the field-level persistence input for an eventual relative saturation or
    19	direct-limit construction.  It does not itself construct the relative high-window
    20	modules over the carve-chart ring.
    21	-/
    22	
    23	set_option autoImplicit false
    24	
    25	universe u
    26

    38	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
    39	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    40	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    41	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    42	  [QuasiCompact (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    43	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 0)]
    44	  [Module.Finite K (Sheaf.HModule (Y.moduleKSheaf K) 1)]
    45	
    46	/-- Multiplication persistence is uniform in the high-window index.  The hypotheses
    47	are exactly the abstract P-fib window pack at `N` and `S`; at `N + n • S` all degree
    48	and normalization inequalities follow from the original ones. -/
    49	theorem mulSpan_divisorSections_highWindow_of_pack
    50	    (g : ℕ) (hO : Sheaf.h0 (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1)
    51	    (hχ : Sheaf.chi (Y.moduleKSheaf K) = 1 - (g : ℤ))
    52	    (N S : Y.CurveDivisor) (β : ℤ)
    53	    (hvan : ∀ W : Y.CurveDivisor, β ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K W →
    54	      Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K W) 1))
    55	    (hNdeg : 2 * (g : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K N)
    56	    (hSdeg : 2 * (g : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K S)
    57	    (hβS : β + 2 * (g : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K S)
    58	    (hβN : β + 2 * (g : ℤ) + CurveDivisor.deg K S ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K N)
    59	    (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (hD0 : 0 ≤ D)
    60	    (hDdeg : CurveDivisor.deg K D = (g : ℤ)) (n : ℕ) :
    61	    Scheme.mulSpan K (divisorSections K S ⊤)
    62	        (divisorSections K (N + n • S - D) ⊤) =
    63	      divisorSections K (N + (n + 1) • S - D) ⊤ := by
    64	  classical
    65	  let Nn : Y.CurveDivisor := N + n • S
    66	  have hSdeg0 : 0 ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K S := by omega
    67	  have hNndeg : CurveDivisor.deg K Nn =
    68	      CurveDivisor.deg K N + (n : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K S := by
    69	    dsimp [Nn]
    70	    rw [CurveDivisor.deg_add, Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_nsmul']
    71	  have hβNn : β + 2 * (g : ℤ) + CurveDivisor.deg K S ≤
    72	      CurveDivisor.deg K Nn := by
    73	    rw [hNndeg]
    74	    have hn : 0 ≤ (n : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K S :=
    75	      mul_nonneg (Int.natCast_nonneg n) hSdeg0
    76	    omega
    77	  have hNnDeg : 2 * (g : ℤ) ≤ CurveDivisor.deg K Nn := by
    78	    rw [hNndeg]
    79	    have hn : 0 ≤ (n : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K S :=
    80	      mul_nonneg (Int.natCast_nonneg n) hSdeg0
    81	    omega
    82	  have hNnNorm : ∀ D' : Y.CurveDivisor,
    83	      CurveDivisor.deg K D' ≤ 2 * (g : ℤ) →
    84	        Subsingleton (Sheaf.HModule (Y.divisorSheaf K (Nn - D')) 1) := by
    85	    intro D' hD'
    86	    apply hvan
    87	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.deg_sub' K, hNndeg]
    88	    have hn : 0 ≤ (n : ℤ) * CurveDivisor.deg K S :=
    89	      mul_nonneg (Int.natCast_nonneg n) hSdeg0
    90	    omega
    91	  let T : Submodule K Y.functionField := divisorSections K (Nn - D) ⊤
    92	  have hTne : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0 :=
    93	    exists_mem_ne_zero_of_window_normalization g hχ Nn hNnNorm hNnDeg D hDdeg rfl
    94	  have hTD : T ≤ divisorSections K Nn ⊤ := by
    95	    refine Scheme.divisorSections_mono K ?_ ⊤
    96	    refine Scheme.CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr fun x hx => ?_
    97	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub]
    98	    have hDx := Scheme.CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mp hD0 x hx
    99	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero] at hDx
   100	    omega
   101	  have hbase : Scheme.baseDivisor K T Nn hTne = D :=
   102	    baseDivisor_window_normalization g hO hχ Nn hNnNorm hNnDeg D hD0 hDdeg rfl hTne
   103	  have hbpf : ∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y),
   104	      ∃ (f : Y.functionField) (_ : f ∈ T) (hf : f ≠ 0),
   105	        coeffAt hx ((Nn - D)
   106	          + Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf)) = 0 := by
   107	    intro x hx
   108	    have h := Scheme.exists_achiever_baseDivisor_sub K hTD hTne hx
   109	    rwa [hbase] at h
   110	  have hspan := mulSpan_eq_divisorSections_of_basepointFree_pack
   111	    g hO hχ Nn S β hvan hSdeg hβS hβNn D hD0 hDdeg.le T
   112	      (by exact le_rfl) 0 (Nat.zero_le g) (by
   113	        simpa only [Nat.add_zero, T] using
   114	          (finrank_divisorSections_top K (Nn - D))) hbpf
   115	  simpa only [T, Nn, add_nsmul, one_nsmul, add_assoc] using hspan
   116	
   117	end Pack

    71	/-- The quotient by the recursively generated relation module at a high window. -/

    79	-- The fully expanded high-window source and fibre kernel exceed the default elaboration budget.
    80	/-- The precise relative persistence condition on a proposed syzygy module for one
    81	successor multiplication presentation. -/
    82	def DivUniversalHighWindowSyzygySpans (n : Nat)

    85	        (r1 := r1) (r2 := r2) (b1 := b1) (b2 := b2) (i := i) (j := j) n))

    11	/-!
    12	# Unit generation by a finite theta-window basis
    13	
    14	The two canonical relative theta sections `(t₀ᵃ, 1)` and `(1, t₁ᵃ)` have a unit
    15	component on the second and first pinned charts respectively.  Pulling either section
    16	back through `relThetaWindowEquiv` and expanding it in a base-changed finite basis shows
    17	that the corresponding chart readings of that basis generate `1`.
    18	-/
    19	
    20	set_option autoImplicit false
    21	set_option backward.isDefEq.respectTransparency false

    35	section Basis
    36	
    37	variable {k R M B : Type u} {ι : Type v} [Field k] [CommRing R] [Algebra k R]
    38	variable [AddCommGroup M] [Module k M] [CommRing B] [Algebra R B]
    39	variable [Fintype ι]
    40	
    41	/-- If an `R`-linear map out of `R ⊗[k] M` takes some element to `1`, then the
    42	images of the scalar extensions of a finite `k`-basis of `M` generate `1` in `B`. -/
    43	theorem exists_basis_baseChange_mul_eq_one (basis : Module.Basis ι k M)
    44	    (f : R ⊗[k] M →ₗ[R] B) (x : R ⊗[k] M) (hx : f x = 1) :
    45	    ∃ c : ι → B, ∑ t, c t * f (1 ⊗ₜ basis t) = 1 := by
    46	  classical
    47	  let basisR := basis.baseChange R
    48	  refine ⟨fun t => (basisR.repr x t) • 1, ?_⟩
    49	  calc
    50	    ∑ t, ((basisR.repr x t) • 1) * f (1 ⊗ₜ basis t) =
    51	        ∑ t, (basisR.repr x t) • f (basisR t) := by
    52	      apply Finset.sum_congr rfl
    53	      intro t _
    54	      simp only [basisR, Module.Basis.baseChange_apply, Algebra.smul_def, mul_one]
    55	    _ = f (∑ t, (basisR.repr x t) • basisR t) := by
    56	      rw [map_sum]
    57	      simp only [map_smul]
    58	    _ = f x := by rw [basisR.sum_repr]
    59	    _ = 1 := hx
    60	
    61	end Basis

    76	/-- The window equivalence followed by the pinned-chart component reading. -/
    77	noncomputable def relThetaWindowChartRead

    79	    (b : Bool) :
    80	    R ⊗[k] ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤) →ₗ[R]

    83	
    84	/-- The readings of any finite basis of a theta window generate `1` on either pinned
    85	chart after scalar extension. -/
    86	theorem exists_basis_relThetaWindowChartRead_mul_eq_one {ι : Type v} [Fintype ι]
    87	    (basis : Module.Basis ι k
    88	      ↥(Scheme.divisorSections k (a • fiberWeilDivisor π) ⊤))
    89	    (hH1 : Subsingleton (relTwistPair C k π (relThetaCocycle C k π a)).H1)
    90	    (b : Bool) :
    91	    ∃ c : ι → Γ(relCurve C R, relPinnedChart C R π b),
    92	      ∑ t, c t * relThetaWindowChartRead C R π a hH1 b (1 ⊗ₜ basis t) = 1 := by
    93	  cases b
    94	  · apply exists_basis_baseChange_mul_eq_one basis
    95	      (relThetaWindowChartRead C R π a hH1 false)
    96	      ((relThetaWindowEquiv C R π a hH1).symm (relThetaSectionSnd C R π a))
    97	    change relThetaResFst a (le_inf le_top le_rfl)
    98	      ((relThetaWindowEquiv C R π a hH1)
    99	        ((relThetaWindowEquiv C R π a hH1).symm (relThetaSectionSnd C R π a))) = 1
   100	    rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
   101	    exact relThetaResFst_relThetaSectionSnd C R π a
   102	  · apply exists_basis_baseChange_mul_eq_one basis
   103	      (relThetaWindowChartRead C R π a hH1 true)
   104	      ((relThetaWindowEquiv C R π a hH1).symm (relThetaSectionFst C R π a))
   105	    change relThetaResSnd a (le_inf le_top le_rfl)
   106	      ((relThetaWindowEquiv C R π a hH1)
   107	        ((relThetaWindowEquiv C R π a hH1).symm (relThetaSectionFst C R π a))) = 1
   108	    rw [LinearEquiv.apply_symm_apply]
   109	    exact relThetaResSnd_relThetaSectionFst C R π a

    10	/-!
    11	# FLV-1 — the twist lattices of `𝒪(D + n·F)` on the π-two-cover
    12	
    13	This is the Wave-4 **fibrewise-large-twist-vanishing** lattice brick (`informal/w4-flv-worksheet.md`
    14	§2.1, brick FLV-1). It records, as *submodule identities in the function field* `K(Y)` (the D1
    15	discipline), how the section lattices of the twisted divisor sheaf `𝒪(D + n·F)` behave on the
    16	pinned affine two-cover `V₀ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₀)`, `V₁ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₁)`, where `F = fiberWeilDivisor π` is the
    17	fiber divisor of FLV-0 and `u = fiberCoordUnit π` its equation:
    18	
    19	* over `V₁` and over the overlap `V₀ ⊓ V₁` the lattice is **unchanged** (`= 𝒪(D)`), since `F`
    20	  is supported off `V₁` (`divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_chart₁`,
    21	  `..._overlap`);
    22	* over `V₀` the lattice is `u⁻ⁿ · 𝒪(D)(V₀)` (the `mulEquivDivisorSheaf` mechanism, section level:
    23	  `divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_chart₀`), a submodule that **grows** with `n`.
    24	
    25	From these the two-cover Čech `H¹` denominators
    26	`Aₙ := 𝒪(D)(V₁)|N ⊔ (u⁻ⁿ · 𝒪(D)(V₀))|N` inside `N := 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)` form an **increasing chain**
    27	(`fiberLattice_mono`) that **exhausts** `N` (`iSup_fiberLattice`) — the pole-clearing at the finite
    28	fiber over `[1 : 0]` — which is the endgame the exhaustion brick (FLV-3) consumes.
    29	-/

    45	variable {K : Type u} [Field K] {Y : Scheme.{u}} [IsIntegral Y]
    46	  [Y.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    47	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    48	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

    52	/-! ## Coefficient bookkeeping for the twist -/
    53	
    54	/-- The coefficient of an `ℕ`-multiple of a divisor scales linearly. -/
    55	private lemma coeffAt_nsmul (n : ℕ) (D : Y.CurveDivisor) {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) :
    56	    coeffAt hx (n • D) = (n : ℤ) * coeffAt hx D := by
    57	  induction n with
    58	  | zero => rw [zero_smul, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, Nat.cast_zero, zero_mul]
    59	  | succ m ih => rw [succ_nsmul, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, ih, Nat.cast_succ]; ring
    60	
    61	/-- The divisor bound depends only on the coefficient at the point. -/
    62	private lemma divisorBound_congr {A B : Y.CurveDivisor} {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y)
    63	    (h : coeffAt hx A = coeffAt hx B) : Scheme.divisorBound A hx = Scheme.divisorBound B hx :=
    64	  congrArg (fun m : Multiplicative ℤ => (m : WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)))
    65	    (congrArg Multiplicative.ofAdd h)
    66	
    67	/-- On `V₁` the twisted divisor `D + n·F` has the same coefficients as `D`: `F` vanishes there. -/
    68	private lemma coeffAt_add_nsmul_of_mem_chart₁ (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) {x : Y}
    69	    (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) (hxV₁ : x ∈ fiberChart₁ π) :
    70	    coeffAt hx (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) = coeffAt hx D := by
    71	  rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, coeffAt_nsmul,
    72	    fiberWeilDivisor_coeffAt_of_mem_chart₁ π hx hxV₁, mul_zero, add_zero]
    73	
    74	/-! ## The constant lattices: over `V₁` and over the overlap -/
    75	
    76	/-- **The lattice over `V₁` is unchanged by the twist.** Since `F` is supported off `V₁`, the
    77	sections of `𝒪(D + n·F)` over `V₁ = π⁻¹ D₊(X₁)` coincide with those of `𝒪(D)`. -/
    78	theorem divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_chart₁ (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
    79	    divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₁ π)
    80	      = divisorSections K D (fiberChart₁ π) := by
    81	  have hne : (fiberChart₁ π : Set Y).Nonempty :=
    82	    ⟨genericPoint Y, (genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π).2⟩
    83	  rw [divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne, divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne]
    84	  have hbound : ∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), x ∈ fiberChart₁ π →
    85	      Scheme.divisorBound (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) hx = Scheme.divisorBound D hx :=
    86	    fun x hx hxV₁ => divisorBound_congr hx (coeffAt_add_nsmul_of_mem_chart₁ π D n hx hxV₁)
    87	  refine Submodule.ext (fun g => ?_)
    88	  rw [mem_boundedSections, mem_boundedSections]
    89	  constructor
    90	  · intro h x hx hxU; rw [← hbound x hx hxU]; exact h x hx hxU
    91	  · intro h x hx hxU; rw [hbound x hx hxU]; exact h x hx hxU
    92	
    93	/-- **The lattice over the overlap is unchanged by the twist.** The overlap `V₀ ⊓ V₁` lies in `V₁`,
    94	where `F` vanishes, so `𝒪(D + n·F)(V₀ ⊓ V₁) = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁) =: N`, the fixed ambient of the Čech
    95	`H¹` quotient. -/
    96	theorem divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
    97	    divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π)
    98	      = divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π) := by
    99	  have hne : ((fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π : Y.Opens) : Set Y).Nonempty :=
   100	    ⟨genericPoint Y, genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π⟩
   101	  rw [divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne, divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne]
   102	  have hbound : ∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), x ∈ fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π →
   103	      Scheme.divisorBound (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) hx = Scheme.divisorBound D hx :=
   104	    fun x hx hxU => divisorBound_congr hx (coeffAt_add_nsmul_of_mem_chart₁ π D n hx hxU.2)
   105	  refine Submodule.ext (fun g => ?_)
   106	  rw [mem_boundedSections, mem_boundedSections]
   107	  constructor
   108	  · intro h x hx hxU; rw [← hbound x hx hxU]; exact h x hx hxU
   109	  · intro h x hx hxU; rw [hbound x hx hxU]; exact h x hx hxU

   111	/-! ## The growing lattice over `V₀` -/
   112	
   113	/-- The classical order of `v⁻¹` is the negative of that of `v`, coefficient-wise. -/
   114	private lemma coeffAt_divOf_inv (v : Y.functionFieldˣ) {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) :
   115	    coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v⁻¹) =
   116	      - coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v) := by
   117	  have h : Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v⁻¹
   118	      + Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v = 0 := by
   119	    rw [← Scheme.divOf_mul (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)), inv_mul_cancel,
   120	      Scheme.divOf_one (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
   121	  have hc := congrArg (coeffAt hx) h
   122	  rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero] at hc
   123	  linarith
   124	
   125	/-- The classical order of `vⁿ` scales linearly. -/
   126	private lemma coeffAt_divOf_pow (v : Y.functionFieldˣ) (n : ℕ) {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) :
   127	    coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (v ^ n)) =
   128	      (n : ℤ) * coeffAt hx (Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) v) := by
   129	  induction n with
   130	  | zero => rw [pow_zero, Scheme.divOf_one, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, Nat.cast_zero, zero_mul]
   131	  | succ m ih =>
   132	    rw [pow_succ, Scheme.divOf_mul, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, ih, Nat.cast_succ]; ring
   133	
   134	/-- **The lattice over `V₀` grows as `u⁻ⁿ · 𝒪(D)(V₀)`.** Multiplication by `u⁻ⁿ = fiberCoordUnit π
   135	⁻ⁿ` carries `𝒪(D)(V₀)` isomorphically onto `𝒪(D + n·F)(V₀)`: the `mulEquivDivisorSheaf` mechanism
   136	at the section level, the source of the growing denominator of the Čech `H¹` quotient. -/
   137	theorem divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_chart₀ (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
   138	    divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₀ π)
   139	      = Submodule.map (mulByUnit K ((fiberCoordUnit π)⁻¹ ^ n)).toLinearMap
   140	          (divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π)) := by
   141	  have hne : (fiberChart₀ π : Set Y).Nonempty :=
   142	    ⟨genericPoint Y, (genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π).1⟩
   143	  set w : Y.functionFieldˣ := (fiberCoordUnit π)⁻¹ ^ n with hw
   144	  -- coefficientwise, `D + n·F` agrees with `D - div w` on `V₀`.
   145	  have hcoeff : ∀ (x : Y) (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y), x ∈ fiberChart₀ π →
   146	      coeffAt hx (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)
   147	        = coeffAt hx (D - Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) w) := by
   148	    intro x hx hxV₀
   149	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, coeffAt_nsmul, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub, hw,
   150	      coeffAt_divOf_pow, coeffAt_divOf_inv,
   151	      fiberWeilDivisor_coeffAt_of_mem_chart₀ π hx hxV₀]
   152	    ring
   153	  -- hence the two bounded lattices coincide.
   154	  have hbdd : Scheme.boundedSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₀ π)
   155	      = Scheme.boundedSections K (D - Scheme.divOf (Y ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) w)
   156	        (fiberChart₀ π) := by
   157	    refine Submodule.ext (fun g => ?_)
   158	    rw [Scheme.mem_boundedSections, Scheme.mem_boundedSections]
   159	    refine forall_congr' (fun x => forall_congr' (fun hx => imp_congr_right (fun hxV₀ => ?_)))
   160	    rw [divisorBound_congr hx (hcoeff x hx hxV₀)]
   161	  rw [divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne, hbdd]
   162	  -- multiplication by `w` identifies `𝒪(D - div w)(V₀)` with `w · 𝒪(D)(V₀)`.
   163	  refine Submodule.ext (fun y => ?_)
   164	  rw [Submodule.mem_map]
   165	  constructor
   166	  · intro hy
   167	    refine ⟨(↑w⁻¹ : Y.functionField) * y, ?_, ?_⟩
   168	    · rw [divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne, ← Scheme.mem_boundedSections_mul_iff K w D,
   169	        ← mul_assoc, Units.mul_inv, one_mul]
   170	      exact hy
   171	    · simp only [Scheme.mulByUnit_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe, ← mul_assoc, Units.mul_inv, one_mul]
   172	  · rintro ⟨h, hh, rfl⟩
   173	    rw [divisorSections_of_nonempty K hne] at hh
   174	    simp only [Scheme.mulByUnit_apply, LinearEquiv.coe_coe]
   175	    exact (Scheme.mem_boundedSections_mul_iff K w D (h : Y.functionField)).mpr hh
   176	
   177	/-! ## The Čech-`H¹` denominator lattice `Aₙ` and its ladder -/
   178	
   179	/-- **The two-cover Čech `H¹` denominator lattice** `Aₙ` of `𝒪(D + n·F)`: the join, inside the
   180	function field, of the section lattices over `V₀` and `V₁`. As submodules of `N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)`
   181	(`fiberLattice_le_overlap`) these are exactly the images of the restriction maps of the two-cover
   182	Čech complex, so `N ⧸ Aₙ` is the two-cover `H¹` (the identification the exhaustion endgame,
   183	FLV-3, consumes). -/
   184	noncomputable def fiberLattice (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) : Submodule K Y.functionField :=
   185	  divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₀ π)
   186	    ⊔ divisorSections K (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π) (fiberChart₁ π)
   187	
   188	/-- **`Aₙ` lies in the ambient `N = 𝒪(D)(V₀ ⊓ V₁)`.** Both section lattices restrict into the
   189	overlap sections, which the twist leaves fixed (`..._overlap`). -/
   190	theorem fiberLattice_le_overlap (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
   191	    fiberLattice π D n ≤ divisorSections K D (fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π) := by
   192	  have hov : ((fiberChart₀ π ⊓ fiberChart₁ π : Y.Opens) : Set Y).Nonempty :=
   193	    ⟨genericPoint Y, genericPoint_mem_preimage_inf π⟩
   194	  refine sup_le ?_ ?_
   195	  · refine (divisorSections_antitone K inf_le_left hov).trans ?_
   196	    rw [divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap π D n]
   197	  · refine (divisorSections_antitone K inf_le_right hov).trans ?_
   198	    rw [divisorSections_add_nsmul_fiberWeilDivisor_overlap π D n]
   199	
   200	/-- **The lattice ladder is increasing.** `Aₙ ≤ Aₙ₊₁`: over `V₀` the twist bound relaxes (`F` is
   201	effective, so `D + n·F ≤ D + (n+1)·F`), and over `V₁` the lattice is constant. -/
   202	theorem fiberLattice_mono (D : Y.CurveDivisor) (n : ℕ) :
   203	    fiberLattice π D n ≤ fiberLattice π D (n + 1) := by
   204	  have hle : D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π ≤ D + (n + 1) • fiberWeilDivisor π := by
   205	    refine Finsupp.le_def.mpr (fun p => ?_)
   206	    change coeffAt p.2 (D + n • fiberWeilDivisor π)
   207	      ≤ coeffAt p.2 (D + (n + 1) • fiberWeilDivisor π)
   208	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, coeffAt_nsmul, coeffAt_nsmul]
   209	    have hF : 0 ≤ coeffAt p.2 (fiberWeilDivisor π) := by
   210	      rw [fiberWeilDivisor_coeffAt π p.2]; exact le_max_right _ _
   211	    have hmul : (n : ℤ) * coeffAt p.2 (fiberWeilDivisor π)
   212	        ≤ ((n : ℤ) + 1) * coeffAt p.2 (fiberWeilDivisor π) :=
   213	      mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right (by linarith) hF
   214	    push_cast
   215	    linarith
   216	  refine sup_le_sup ?_ ?_
   217	  · exact divisorSections_mono K hle (fiberChart₀ π)
   218	  · exact divisorSections_mono K hle (fiberChart₁ π)
   219	
   220	/-! ## Exhaustion of `N` by the ladder -/
   221	
   222	/-- The divisor bound `≤`-comparison at a point reduces to the pointwise coefficient
   223	`≤`-comparison in `ℤ`. -/
   224	private lemma divisorBound_le_iff {A B : Y.CurveDivisor} {x : Y} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint Y) :
   225	    Scheme.divisorBound A hx ≤ Scheme.divisorBound B hx ↔ coeffAt hx A ≤ coeffAt hx B := by
   226	  simp only [Scheme.divisorBound, WithZero.coe_le_coe, Multiplicative.ofAdd_le]
   227	  rfl
   228	
   229	/-- Membership of a *nonzero* rational function `s` in a bounded lattice, read through its
   230	principal divisor: `s ∈ 𝒪(A)(U)` iff `-div(s) ≤ A` at every point of `U`. -/
   231	private lemma mem_boundedSections_unit_iff (s : Y.functionFieldˣ) (A : Y.CurveDivisor)
   232	    (U : Y.Opens) :

     8	/-!
     9	# DD-F brick 1 — the base divisor of a subspace of `H⁰(𝒪(A))`
    10	
    11	The normalization vocabulary of the P-fib route (`informal/dat-d-worksheet.md` §3.3 F1,
    12	`informal/dd-f-probe-verdict.md` inventory brick 1): for a subspace `T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A))` of the
    13	global sections of a divisor sheaf with a nonzero element, the **base divisor**
    14	`bd(T) = ∑ₓ min_{0 ≠ f ∈ T} (A + div f)ₓ · x` records, at each closed point, the deepest
    15	common zero of the shifted divisors `A + div f ≥ 0`. Provided:
    16	
    17	* `Scheme.baseDivisorAt` — the pointwise minimum, as a `ℕ`-valued `sInf` (well-defined
    18	  since `T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A))` makes every `A + div f` effective);
    19	* `Scheme.baseDivisor` — the assembled Weil divisor, finitely supported because it is
    20	  bounded by any one `A + div f₀`;
    21	* `baseDivisor_nonneg`, `coeffAt_baseDivisor` — effectivity and the pointwise value;
    22	* `baseDivisorAt_le_coeffAt` — the lower-bound property (`bd(T) ≤ A + div f` for every
    23	  nonzero `f ∈ T`);
    24	* `exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt` — the **achiever**: at every closed point some
    25	  nonzero `f ∈ T` attains the minimum (`Nat.sInf_mem`);
    26	* `le_divisorSections_sub_baseDivisor` — `T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A − bd T))`;
    27	* `exists_achiever_baseDivisor_sub` — **no residual base point**: relative to
    28	  `A − bd T`, the subspace `T` has an exact-order element at every closed point. This is
    29	  the `hbpf` input of the bpf-span lemma (F3-core).
    30	
    31	Everything is `ord`/`coeffAt` calculus on `mem_divisorSections_top_iff`; no cohomology.
    32	-/
    33	
    34	set_option autoImplicit false
    35	
    36	universe u
    37	
    38	open CategoryTheory Limits Opposite TopologicalSpace
    39	
    40	attribute [local instance] AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.functionFieldOverModule
    41	  AlgebraicGeometry.Scheme.overModule
    42	
    43	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
    44	
    45	open Scheme
    46	
    47	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    48	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] [IsIntegral X]
    49	  [LocallyOfFiniteType (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    50	  [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]
    51	
    52	/-! ## The pointwise minimum -/
    53	
    54	/-- The candidate multiplicities of the base divisor of `T` relative to `A` at the closed
    55	point `p`: the values `(A + div f)ₚ` over nonzero `f ∈ T`, truncated to `ℕ` (faithful once
    56	`T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A))`, which makes every `A + div f` effective). -/
    57	def Scheme.baseDivisorSet (T : Submodule K X.functionField) (A : X.CurveDivisor)
    58	    (p : {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X}) : Set ℕ :=
    59	  {n : ℕ | ∃ (f : X.functionField) (_ : f ∈ T) (hf : f ≠ 0),
    60	    (coeffAt p.2
    61	      (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))).toNat = n}
    62	
    63	/-- **The base multiplicity of `T` relative to `A` at a closed point**: the minimum of
    64	`(A + div f)ₚ` over nonzero `f ∈ T`. -/
    65	noncomputable def Scheme.baseDivisorAt (T : Submodule K X.functionField)
    66	    (A : X.CurveDivisor) (p : {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X}) : ℕ :=
    67	  sInf (Scheme.baseDivisorSet K T A p)
    68	
    69	lemma Scheme.baseDivisorSet_nonempty {T : Submodule K X.functionField}
    70	    (A : X.CurveDivisor) (hT : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0) (p : {x : X // x ≠ genericPoint X}) :
    71	    (Scheme.baseDivisorSet K T A p).Nonempty := by
    72	  obtain ⟨f, hfT, hf⟩ := hT
    73	  exact ⟨_, f, hfT, hf, rfl⟩
    74	
    75	/-! ## The assembled base divisor -/
    76	
    77	/-- **The base divisor `bd(T)` of a subspace `T` relative to `A`**: the Weil divisor of
    78	pointwise base multiplicities. Finitely supported because `0 ≤ bd(T)ₚ ≤ (A + div f₀)ₚ`
    79	for the chosen nonzero `f₀ ∈ T`. -/
    80	noncomputable def Scheme.baseDivisor (T : Submodule K X.functionField)
    81	    (A : X.CurveDivisor) (hT : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0) : X.CurveDivisor :=
    82	  Finsupp.onFinset
    83	    (toFinsupp (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
    84	      (Units.mk0 hT.choose hT.choose_spec.2))).support
    85	    (fun p => (Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A p : ℤ))
    86	    (fun p hp => by
    87	      rw [Finsupp.mem_support_iff]
    88	      intro hzero
    89	      apply hp
    90	      have hle : Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A p
    91	          ≤ (coeffAt p.2 (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
    92	              (Units.mk0 hT.choose hT.choose_spec.2))).toNat :=
    93	        Nat.sInf_le ⟨hT.choose, hT.choose_spec.1, hT.choose_spec.2, rfl⟩
    94	      have hc : coeffAt p.2 (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))
    95	          (Units.mk0 hT.choose hT.choose_spec.2)) = 0 := hzero
    96	      omega)
    97	
    98	/-- The pointwise value of the base divisor is the base multiplicity. -/
    99	lemma Scheme.coeffAt_baseDivisor {T : Submodule K X.functionField} {A : X.CurveDivisor}
   100	    (hT : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0) {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
   101	    coeffAt hx (Scheme.baseDivisor K T A hT)
   102	      = (Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A ⟨x, hx⟩ : ℤ) :=
   103	  rfl
   104	
   105	/-- **The base divisor is effective.** -/
   106	lemma Scheme.baseDivisor_nonneg {T : Submodule K X.functionField} {A : X.CurveDivisor}
   107	    (hT : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0) : 0 ≤ Scheme.baseDivisor K T A hT := by
   108	  refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun x hx => ?_)
   109	  rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, Scheme.coeffAt_baseDivisor K hT hx]
   110	  positivity
   111	
   112	/-! ## The lower-bound and achiever properties -/
   113	
   114	/-- Under `T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A))`, the shifted divisor `A + div f` of a nonzero `f ∈ T` is
   115	effective at every closed point. -/
   116	lemma Scheme.coeffAt_add_divOf_nonneg {T : Submodule K X.functionField}
   117	    {A : X.CurveDivisor} (hTA : T ≤ divisorSections K A ⊤) {f : X.functionField}
   118	    (hfT : f ∈ T) (hf : f ≠ 0) {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
   119	    0 ≤ coeffAt hx
   120	      (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf)) := by
   121	  have hmem := hTA hfT
   122	  rw [mem_divisorSections_top_iff K hf] at hmem
   123	  have h := CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mp hmem x hx
   124	  rwa [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero] at h
   125	
   126	/-- **The lower-bound property of the base divisor**: `bd(T) ≤ A + div f` pointwise, for
   127	every nonzero `f ∈ T`. -/
   128	lemma Scheme.baseDivisorAt_le_coeffAt {T : Submodule K X.functionField}
   129	    {A : X.CurveDivisor} (hTA : T ≤ divisorSections K A ⊤) {f : X.functionField}
   130	    (hfT : f ∈ T) (hf : f ≠ 0) {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
   131	    (Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A ⟨x, hx⟩ : ℤ)
   132	      ≤ coeffAt hx
   133	          (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf)) := by
   134	  have h1 : Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A ⟨x, hx⟩
   135	      ≤ (coeffAt hx
   136	          (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))).toNat :=
   137	    Nat.sInf_le ⟨f, hfT, hf, rfl⟩
   138	  have h2 := Scheme.coeffAt_add_divOf_nonneg K hTA hfT hf hx
   139	  omega
   140	
   141	/-- **The achiever**: at every closed point, some nonzero `f ∈ T` attains the base
   142	multiplicity: `(A + div f)ₓ = bd(T)ₓ`. -/
   143	lemma Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt {T : Submodule K X.functionField}
   144	    {A : X.CurveDivisor} (hTA : T ≤ divisorSections K A ⊤) (hT : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0)
   145	    {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
   146	    ∃ (f : X.functionField) (_ : f ∈ T) (hf : f ≠ 0),
   147	      coeffAt hx (A + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf))
   148	        = (Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A ⟨x, hx⟩ : ℤ) := by
   149	  have hmem : Scheme.baseDivisorAt K T A ⟨x, hx⟩ ∈ Scheme.baseDivisorSet K T A ⟨x, hx⟩ :=
   150	    Nat.sInf_mem (Scheme.baseDivisorSet_nonempty K A hT ⟨x, hx⟩)
   151	  obtain ⟨f, hfT, hf, heq⟩ := hmem
   152	  refine ⟨f, hfT, hf, ?_⟩
   153	  have h2 := Scheme.coeffAt_add_divOf_nonneg K hTA hfT hf hx
   154	  omega
   155	
   156	/-! ## The normalization: `T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A − bd T))` with no residual base point -/
   157	
   158	/-- **The base-divisor normalization**: `T ⊆ H⁰(𝒪(A − bd T))` — every nonzero `f ∈ T`
   159	has `(A − bd T) + div f ≥ 0` because `bd(T)` is a pointwise minimum. -/
   160	theorem Scheme.le_divisorSections_sub_baseDivisor {T : Submodule K X.functionField}
   161	    {A : X.CurveDivisor} (hTA : T ≤ divisorSections K A ⊤) (hT : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0) :
   162	    T ≤ divisorSections K (A - Scheme.baseDivisor K T A hT) ⊤ := by
   163	  intro f hfT
   164	  by_cases hf : f = 0
   165	  · subst hf
   166	    exact Submodule.zero_mem _
   167	  · rw [mem_divisorSections_top_iff K hf]
   168	    refine CurveDivisor.le_iff_coeffAt.mpr (fun x hx => ?_)
   169	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_zero, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub,
   170	      Scheme.coeffAt_baseDivisor K hT hx]
   171	    have h4 := Scheme.baseDivisorAt_le_coeffAt K hTA hfT hf hx
   172	    rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add] at h4
   173	    omega
   174	
   175	/-- **No residual base point** (the `hbpf` input of the bpf-span lemma): relative to the
   176	normalized divisor `A − bd T`, the subspace `T` has an exact-order element at every
   177	closed point: `((A − bd T) + div f)ₓ = 0`. -/
   178	theorem Scheme.exists_achiever_baseDivisor_sub {T : Submodule K X.functionField}
   179	    {A : X.CurveDivisor} (hTA : T ≤ divisorSections K A ⊤) (hT : ∃ f ∈ T, f ≠ 0)
   180	    {x : X} (hx : x ≠ genericPoint X) :
   181	    ∃ (f : X.functionField) (_ : f ∈ T) (hf : f ≠ 0),
   182	      coeffAt hx ((A - Scheme.baseDivisor K T A hT)
   183	        + Scheme.divOf (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) (Units.mk0 f hf)) = 0 := by
   184	  obtain ⟨f, hfT, hf, heq⟩ := Scheme.exists_coeffAt_eq_baseDivisorAt K hTA hT hx
   185	  refine ⟨f, hfT, hf, ?_⟩
   186	  rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add, CurveDivisor.coeffAt_sub,
   187	    Scheme.coeffAt_baseDivisor K hT hx]
   188	  rw [CurveDivisor.coeffAt_add] at heq
   189	  omega
   190

    10	# Sections to divisors — the LocalEquations construction and the class law (DAT-A)
    11	
    12	Worksheet §2.2 step 2, made literal (`informal/spec-dat-a.md` §3): a global section of
    13	the DAT-1 glued sheaf **is** a matching family `(s_j)` with `s_i = g_{ij}·s_j`, so once
    14	its components are germ-regular (DAT-A2, `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SectionsToDivisors`)
    15	it is a `Scheme.LocalEquations` datum on the nose. The (1e) class law
    16	(`Cohomology/GluedSheafClass.lean`, landed while this brick was in flight) is consumed
    17	directly — the spec's `cocycleClassOn` seam is CLOSED, no interim class carrier exists:
    18	
    19	* `BasicOpenCocycleDatum.sectionLocalEquations` — the LocalEquations datum of a
    20	  germ-regular global section on **any** pointed cover subordinated to the pieces
    21	  (the (1e) subordination interface `𝒲, σ, hσ`): equations the restricted components
    22	  `D.component s (σ y)`, ratio witnesses the subordinated transition units
    23	  `gluedSubordUnit`;
    24	* `sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit` — the ratio units are **exactly** the (restricted)
    25	  transition units of the cocycle (`ratioUnit_unique`); on the piece cover the
    26	  restriction is along `≤`-reflexivity, i.e. the units themselves;
    27	* `sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle` — the units cocycle of the constructed datum is
    28	  the (1e) subordinated cocycle `gluedSubordCocycle`;
    29	* **the class law** `sectionLocalEquations_picClass`:
    30	  `(D.sectionLocalEquations …).picClass = D.cechPicClass` — the divisor datum cut out
    31	  by a germ-regular section presents THE class of the datum's cocycle (the Abel
    32	  correspondence), through the landed `cechPicClass_eq_mk`. Naturality under
    33	  refinement/subordination-choice is the landed `gluedSubordCocycle_class_eq`; unit
    34	  rescalings and cover refinements of the constructed datum keep the class by the
    35	  landed `LocalEquations.picClass_rescale`/`picClass_restrict`;
    36	* `sectionLocalEquations_picClass_congr` — any two germ-regular sections on any two
    37	  subordinated covers cut divisors of the same class;
    38	* `sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular` — the A2-bundled wrapper on the canonical
    39	  pointed cover (`D.pointedCover`): a fibrewise-regular global section yields the
    40	  divisor datum outright, with class `D.cechPicClass` (`[IsNoetherianRing B]`).

    58	/-- The value of a restricted unit section is the restriction of its value. -/
    59	private lemma val_unitsRestrict {X : Scheme.{u}} {W U : X.Opens} (h : W ≤ U)
    60	    (u : Γ(X, U)ˣ) :
    61	    ((X.unitsRestrict h u : Γ(X, W)ˣ) : Γ(X, W)) = X.resHom h (u : Γ(X, U)) :=

    67	variable (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
    68	variable (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
    69	variable (𝒲 : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ : relCurve C B → D.index)
    70	variable (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ y))
    71	
    72	/-- The defining ratio equation of the section's restricted components on the overlaps
    73	of a subordinated pointed cover: the matching relation of the glued family, restricted
    74	from `⊤ ⊓ Uᵢ ⊓ Uⱼ`. -/
    75	private lemma component_ratio_eq (y y' : relCurve C B) :
    76	    ((relCurve C B).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_left :
    77	        𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y)).op).hom
    78	        ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)))
    79	      = (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :
    80	            Γ(relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'))
    81	        * ((relCurve C B).presheaf.map (homOfLE (inf_le_right :
    82	            𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y' ≤ 𝒲.opens y')).op).hom
    83	            ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y') (D.component s (σ y'))) := by
    84	  have hle : 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'
    85	      ≤ ⊤ ⊓ D.pieces (σ y) ⊓ D.pieces (σ y') :=
    86	    le_inf (le_inf le_top (inf_le_left.trans (hσ y))) (inf_le_right.trans (hσ y'))
    87	  have key := congrArg ((relCurve C B).resHom hle) (s.property (σ y) (σ y'))
    88	  rw [map_mul] at key
    89	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom] at key
    90	  change (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_left
    91	      ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y)))
    92	    = (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :
    93	        Γ(relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ⊓ 𝒲.opens y'))
    94	      * (relCurve C B).resHom inf_le_right
    95	          ((relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y') (D.component s (σ y')))
    96	  rw [gluedSubordUnit, val_unitsRestrict, component, component]
    97	  simp only [Scheme.resHom_resHom]
    98	  exact key

   100	/-- **Sections ↦ divisor families** (DAT-A, worksheet §2.2 step 2): a germ-regular
   101	global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf is a `Scheme.LocalEquations` datum on any
   102	pointed cover subordinated to the pieces — the equations are the (restricted)
   103	components, the ratio witnesses the subordinated transition units. Germ-regularity
   104	(`hreg`) is DAT-A2's output (`germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors` relatively;
   105	`Scheme.germ_mem_nonZeroDivisors_of_ne_zero` on an integral field-level curve). -/
   106	noncomputable def sectionLocalEquations
   107	    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
   108	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
   109	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y)) :
   110	    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations where
   111	  cover := 𝒲
   112	  eqn y := (relCurve C B).resHom (hσ y) (D.component s (σ y))
   113	  regular y z hz := by
   114	    rw [Scheme.resHom, TopCat.Presheaf.germ_res_apply]
   115	    exact hreg (σ y) z (hσ y hz)
   116	  ratio_isUnit y y' :=
   117	    ⟨gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y', D.component_ratio_eq s 𝒲 σ hσ y y'⟩
   118	
   119	variable (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),
   120	  ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s j)
   121	    ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y))

   125	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).cover = 𝒲 :=

   132	  rfl

   134	/-- **The ratio units are exactly the cocycle's transition units** (worksheet §2.2 step
   135	2's "ratio units EXACTLY the cocycle"), in subordinated form: by uniqueness of ratio
   136	witnesses against a regular equation. On the piece cover the subordination is
   137	`≤`-reflexivity and `gluedSubordUnit` is the transition unit restricted along it. -/
   138	lemma sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit (y y' : relCurve C B) :

   140	      = gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y' :=
   141	  ((D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).ratioUnit_unique y y'
   142	    (gluedSubordUnit D.unit 𝒲 σ hσ y y')
   143	    (D.component_ratio_eq s 𝒲 σ hσ y y')).symm

   146	cocycle of the datum. -/
   147	lemma sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle :
   148	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle
   149	      = gluedSubordCocycle D.isGluingCocycle 𝒲 σ hσ :=

   152	      ((D.sectionLocalEquations_ratioUnit s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg y y').trans
   153	        (gluedSubordCocycle_evInf D.isGluingCocycle 𝒲 σ hσ y y').symm)

   155	/-- **THE CLASS LAW** (DAT-A keystone; the Abel correspondence of worksheet §2.2 step
   156	2): the Picard class of the divisor datum cut out by a germ-regular global section of
   157	the DAT-1 glued sheaf is THE Čech Picard class of the datum's cocycle (stage (1e),

   161	  change Scheme.CechPic.mk 𝒲
   162	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).unitsCocycle.class = D.cechPicClass
   163	  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_unitsCocycle s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg]

   173	theorem sectionLocalEquations_picClass_congr
   174	    {π : C.left ⟶ P1 k} [IsAffineHom π] (D : BasicOpenCocycleDatum C B π)
   175	    (s s' : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
   176	    (𝒲 𝒲' : (relCurve C B).PointedCover) (σ σ' : relCurve C B → D.index)
   177	    (hσ : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ y))
   178	    (hσ' : ∀ y : relCurve C B, 𝒲'.opens y ≤ D.pieces (σ' y))
   179	    (hreg : ∀ (j : D.index) (y : relCurve C B) (hy : y ∈ D.pieces j),

   181	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y))

   183	      ((relCurve C B).presheaf.germ (D.pieces j) y hy).hom (D.component s' j)
   184	        ∈ nonZeroDivisors ((relCurve C B).presheaf.stalk y)) :
   185	    (D.sectionLocalEquations s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg).picClass
   186	      = (D.sectionLocalEquations s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg').picClass := by
   187	  rw [D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s 𝒲 σ hσ hreg,
   188	    D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s' 𝒲' σ' hσ' hreg']

   197	/-- **Fibrewise-nonzero sections cut divisors** (DAT-A + DAT-A2, bundled): over a
   198	Noetherian test ring, a fibrewise-regular global section of the DAT-1 glued sheaf
   199	yields a `LocalEquations` divisor datum on the canonical pointed cover by pieces; its

   201	noncomputable def sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular
   202	    [IsNoetherianRing B]

   204	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective

   206	    (relCurve C B).LocalEquations :=
   207	  D.sectionLocalEquations s D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl)
   208	    (fun j y hy => D.germ_component_mem_nonZeroDivisors s j (hfib j) y hy)

   211	divisor of class exactly the datum's (1e) class. -/
   212	theorem sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular_picClass
   213	    [IsNoetherianRing B]
   214	    (s : ↥(gluedSubmodule B D.pieces D.unit ⊤))
   215	    (hfib : ∀ (j : D.index) (p : PrimeSpectrum B), Function.Injective
   216	      ((Scheme.mulSectionEnd B (D.component s j)).rTensor p.asIdeal.ResidueField)) :
   217	    (D.sectionLocalEquationsOfFibrewiseRegular s hfib).picClass = D.cechPicClass :=
   218	  D.sectionLocalEquations_picClass s D.pointedCover D.pieceIndex (fun _ => le_rfl) _

    63	variable (K : Type u) [Field K] {X : Scheme.{u}} [X.Over (Spec (CommRingCat.of K))]

    66	/-- **Divisibility in a DVR stalk is valuation comparison** (the engine of the
    67	stalk-ideal ↔ order dictionary): for elements `y, e` of the stalk at a closed point with
    68	`e ≠ 0`, `e ∣ y` exactly when the order of `y` in the function field is at most that of
    69	`e`.  Total divisibility of the valuation ring, with the unit case read off
    70	`valuation_eq_one_iff_notMem`. -/
    71	theorem Scheme.dvd_iff_ord_le {z : X} (hz : z ≠ genericPoint X)
    72	    {y e : X.presheaf.stalk z} :
    73	    e ∣ y ↔
    74	      Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz
    75	          (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField y)
    76	        ≤ Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz
    77	            (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField e) := by
    78	  letI := isDiscreteValuationRing_stalk (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz
    79	  letI := isDedekindDomain_stalk (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz
    80	  have hord : Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz
    81	      = (stalkHeightOne X z).valuation X.functionField := rfl
    82	  rw [hord]
    83	  constructor
    84	  · rintro ⟨c, rfl⟩
    85	    rw [map_mul, Valuation.map_mul]
    86	    exact mul_le_of_le_one_right' ((stalkHeightOne X z).valuation_le_one c)
    87	  · intro hle
    88	    rcases eq_or_ne y 0 with rfl | hy
    89	    · exact dvd_zero e
    90	    rcases ValuationRing.dvd_total e y with hdvd | hdvd
    91	    · exact hdvd
    92	    · -- `y ∣ e`: the cofactor has valuation `1`, hence is a unit
    93	      obtain ⟨c, hc⟩ := hdvd
    94	      have hyne : (stalkHeightOne X z).valuation X.functionField
    95	          (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField y) ≠ 0 := by
    96	        simp only [ne_eq, Valuation.zero_iff]
    97	        exact fun h0 =>
    98	          hy ((map_eq_zero_iff _
    99	            (IsFractionRing.injective (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField)).mp h0)
   100	      have hcge : (1 : WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ))
   101	          ≤ (stalkHeightOne X z).valuation X.functionField
   102	              (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField c) := by
   103	        have he' : (stalkHeightOne X z).valuation X.functionField
   104	            (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField e)
   105	            = (stalkHeightOne X z).valuation X.functionField
   106	                (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField y)
   107	              * (stalkHeightOne X z).valuation X.functionField
   108	                (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField c) := by
   109	          rw [← Valuation.map_mul, ← map_mul, ← hc]
   110	        rw [he'] at hle
   111	        exact (mul_le_mul_iff_right₀ (zero_lt_iff.mpr hyne)).mp (by rwa [mul_one])
   112	      have hcunit : IsUnit c := by
   113	        have h1 : (stalkHeightOne X z).valuation X.functionField
   114	            (algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField c) = 1 :=
   115	          le_antisymm ((stalkHeightOne X z).valuation_le_one c) hcge
   116	        rw [IsDedekindDomain.HeightOneSpectrum.valuation_eq_one_iff_notMem] at h1
   117	        exact IsLocalRing.notMem_maximalIdeal.mp h1
   118	      obtain ⟨u, rfl⟩ := hcunit
   119	      exact ⟨(u⁻¹ : (X.presheaf.stalk z)ˣ), by
   120	        rw [hc, mul_assoc, Units.mul_inv_eq_one.mpr rfl, mul_one]⟩
   121	
   122	/-- **The stalk-ideal ↔ order dictionary** (the pole-bound bridge of the DD-4 field
   123	dictionary): the germ at a closed point `z` of a section `β` lies in the stalk ideal of
   124	the divisor family `d` exactly when the order at `z` of its rational-function reading
   125	`germ_η β` is bounded by the order of `d`'s local equation — i.e. of the trivializing
   126	element `d.presentation.elem z`. -/
   127	theorem Scheme.LocalEquations.germ_mem_stalkIdeal_iff_ord_le (d : X.LocalEquations)
   128	    {U : X.Opens} (hηU : genericPoint X ∈ U) {z : X} (hzU : z ∈ U)
   129	    (hz : z ≠ genericPoint X) (β : Γ(X, U)) :
   130	    (X.presheaf.germ U z hzU).hom β ∈ d.stalkIdeal z ↔
   131	      Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz
   132	          ((X.presheaf.germ U (genericPoint X) hηU).hom β)
   133	        ≤ Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz
   134	            ((d.presentation.elem z : X.functionField)) := by
   135	  have hβ := Scheme.germ_generic_eq_algebraMap_germ hηU hzU β
   136	  have helem : (d.presentation.elem z : X.functionField)
   137	      = algebraMap (X.presheaf.stalk z) X.functionField
   138	          ((X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens z) z (d.cover.mem_opens z)).hom (d.eqn z)) := by
   139	    rw [Scheme.LocalEquations.presentation_elem_val]
   140	    exact Scheme.germ_generic_eq_algebraMap_germ (d.cover.genericPoint_mem_opens z)
   141	      (d.cover.mem_opens z) (d.eqn z)
   142	  rw [Scheme.LocalEquations.stalkIdeal, Ideal.mem_span_singleton, hβ, helem]
   143	  exact Scheme.dvd_iff_ord_le K hz
   144	
   145	/-- **The stalk ideal at the generic point is everything**: the local equation is
   146	regular, so its germ at `η` is a nonzero element of the function *field* — the
   147	generic-point clauses of the vanishing submodule are vacuous. -/
   148	theorem Scheme.LocalEquations.stalkIdeal_genericPoint (d : X.LocalEquations) :
   149	    d.stalkIdeal (genericPoint X) = ⊤ := by
   150	  rw [Scheme.LocalEquations.stalkIdeal, Ideal.span_singleton_eq_top]
   151	  have hne : (X.presheaf.germ (d.cover.opens (genericPoint X)) (genericPoint X)
   152	      (d.cover.mem_opens (genericPoint X))).hom (d.eqn (genericPoint X)) ≠ 0 :=
   153	    mem_nonZeroDivisors_iff_ne_zero.mp
   154	      (d.regular (genericPoint X) (genericPoint X)
   155	        (d.cover.mem_opens (genericPoint X)))
   156	  exact isUnit_iff_ne_zero.mpr hne
   157	
   158	/-- The order of the trivializing element of the presentation of a divisor family is
   159	the divisor bound of the **negated** presentation divisor: `ord_z (elem z)` prescribes
   160	exactly the zero the divisor demands. -/
   161	theorem Scheme.LocalEquations.ord_presentation_elem
   162	    [QuasiCompact (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K))] (d : X.LocalEquations) {z : X}
   163	    (hz : z ≠ genericPoint X) :
   164	    Scheme.ord (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz ((d.presentation.elem z : X.functionField))
   165	      = Scheme.divisorBound (-Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation) hz := by
   166	  rw [← Scheme.coe_inv_ordZ K (d.presentation.elem z) hz]
   167	  have hbound : Scheme.divisorBound (-Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation) hz
   168	      = ((Multiplicative.ofAdd
   169	            (coeffAt hz (-Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation)) :
   170	          Multiplicative ℤ) : WithZero (Multiplicative ℤ)) :=
   171	    rfl
   172	  have hcoeff : coeffAt hz (-Scheme.presentationDivisor K d.presentation)
   173	      = Multiplicative.toAdd
   174	          ((Scheme.ordZ (X ↘ Spec (CommRingCat.of K)) hz (d.presentation.elem z))⁻¹) := by
   175	    rw [Scheme.CurveDivisor.coeffAt_neg hz,
   176	      Scheme.coeffAt_presentationDivisor K d.presentation hz, toAdd_inv]
   177	  rw [hbound, hcoeff, ofAdd_toAdd]
   178	
   179	end StalkOrder

   190	/-- **The deterministic chart selector**: `inl` on the first pinned chart `V₀ᴷ`, `inr`
   191	off it.  Unlike the datum's `pieceIndex` (a `Classical.choose`), the branch is
   192	*provable*: `x ∈ V₀ → thetaFieldChartIndex x = inl`. -/
   193	noncomputable def thetaFieldChartIndex (x : relCurve C K) : (thetaChartCover C K π).index :=
   194	  if x ∈ (relCover C K (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀ then Sum.inl PUnit.unit

   198	    (hx : x ∈ (relCover C K (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀) :
   199	    thetaFieldChartIndex C K π x = Sum.inl PUnit.unit :=
   200	  if_pos hx
   201	
   202	lemma thetaFieldChartIndex_of_notMem {x : relCurve C K}
   203	    (hx : x ∉ (relCover C K (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀) :

   208	lemma mem_V₁_of_notMem_V₀ {x : relCurve C K}
   209	    (hx : x ∉ (relCover C K (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀) :
   210	    x ∈ (relCover C K (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := by
   211	  have hx' : x ∈ (relCover C K (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
   212	      ⊔ (relCover C K (fiberTwoCover π)).V₁ := by rw [relCover_sup]; trivial
   213	  rcases (TopologicalSpace.Opens.mem_sup).mp hx' with h0 | h1

   218	    x ∈ (thetaChartCover C K π).pieces (thetaFieldChartIndex C K π x) := by
   219	  by_cases hx : x ∈ (relCover C K (fiberTwoCover π)).V₀
   220	  · rw [thetaFieldChartIndex_of_mem C K π hx, thetaChartCover_pieces_inl]
